blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from Jared's verified local notes (researched November 1, 2026). Listing-stated figures are labelled; unconfirmed items say so. No live listing feed or board statistics are attached to this page yet.

Edgemont Village is a neighbourhood in the District of North Vancouver and one of the District's six Village Centres (with Lions Gate, Queensdale, Maplewood, Parkgate and Deep Cove) in its Upper Capilano area; its core is the Edgemont Boulevard shopping strip at Highland Boulevard, where the Capilano Library (3045 Highland Boulevard) sits — described by the library as "located in the heart of Edgemont Village." Nearby areas: Canyon Heights (west), Capilano Highlands (north), Delbrook and Upper Lonsdale (east), Queensdale (southeast).
This guide covers Edgemont's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
Condo buildings in Edgemont
Edgemont (Edgemont Village) is in the District of North Vancouver — NOT the City of North Vancouver. Its governing bylaws are OCP Bylaw 7900 and Zoning Bylaw 3210.

Connaught (Grosvenor Edgemont) — 3230 Connaught Crescent (project address per the developer/presale sources; current listings for individual units use 3220 Connaught Crescent — both numbers are in public use for the same project)

A concrete mixed-use project by Grosvenor over ground-floor retail anchored by Thrifty Foods (with Shoppers Drug Mart among the retailers), comprising 82 homes in total: 59 apartments and 23 townhomes (building-directory project source, reconciling with Grosvenor's own "82 high-quality concrete condominiums and townhomes"); an NVRC document counts the wider grocery-site project at 83 apartments and townhomes — the one-home difference is not confirmed between those sources and does not affect the 59-apartment figure both frames support. Construction commenced 2016 and completed 2019 per Grosvenor — the homes are resales, not presales. A current listing records a 2019-built Apartment/Condo unit in the project with strata fees, cats OK in listing data, bike room and exercise centre among amenities. No source states any age restriction — general-market, verified NOT 55+ in the 55+ pass. Published rental restrictions: Not confirmed (and any long-term rental ban would be VOID since November 24, 2022 —). (55+ notes
Edgemont Villa — 3151 Connaught Crescent (Edgemont Village)

The village's verified age-restricted strata: freehold strata, built 2003, with only 20 condos per a listing feature sheet; multiple listings describe it in the same terms as a "boutique 55+ residence" / "55+ building" in the heart of Edgemont Village, with underground parking (1 stall per listing), elevator and storage, and amenities including electricity, trash, maintenance grounds, hot water and water in listing data. Age restriction: 55+ — listing-stated; the exact bylaw wording is a Form B item and must be confirmed in the strata documents (Form B / bylaws) before relying on it. Pet restrictions: Not confirmed from the sources checked. Counted once, here, as a strata condo with its 55+ position noted. (55+ notes
Crescentview at Edgemont — 3121 Connaught Crescent

A 3-storey wood-frame low-rise by VPAC Construction Group, designed by RLA Architects, completed 2023, comprising 22 residential condominiums (1- to 3-bedroom, 744–1,155 sq ft per the presale source) at the edge of the village retail hub. Published policy: the project source states short-term rentals like Airbnb are not permitted under current policies — a strata bylaw item, confirm on the Form B. Pet restrictions and long-term rental position beyond that statement: Not confirmed (a long-term rental ban would in any case be VOID since November 24, 2022). No source states any age restriction — general-market.

items.t: Edgemont Village is a neighbourhood in the District of North Vancouver and one of the District's six Village Centres (with Lions Gate, Queensdale, Maplewood, Parkgate and Deep Cove) in its Upper Capilano area; its core is the Edgemont Boulevard shopping strip at Highland Boulevard, where the Capilano Library (3045 Highland Boulevard) sits — described by the library as "located in the heart of Edgemont Village." Nearby areas: Canyon Heights (west), Capilano Highlands (north), Delbrook and Upper Lonsdale (east), Queensdale (southeast).

Where condo stock concentrates: entirely in and immediately around the village core, on one short crescent. All three counted buildings stand on Connaught Crescent within a few blocks of the Edgemont Boulevard strip — Edgemont Villa (3151), Crescentview (3121) and Connaught (3220/3230) — because attached housing in Edgemont is concentrated in and immediately around the village core, while the surrounding plateau between Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek is predominantly freehold detached homes.
Catchments for any other Edgemont address — including the Connaught Crescent buildings — are not verified per address.

Transit: TransLink Route 232 (Grouse Mountain/Phibbs Exchange) runs through the village via Highland Boulevard, Edgemont Boulevard and Capilano Road; Route 246 (Downtown/Highland) runs via Capilano Road, Ridgewood Drive, Edgemont Boulevard and Highland Boulevard, with downtown-bound trips crossing the Lions Gate Bridge. The SeaBus from Lonsdale Quay crosses to Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day.

Village redevelopment frame: the Grosvenor Edgemont project redeveloped the village's main grocery site at the Edgemont/Ridgewood gateway — a low-density mixed-use project with an expanded grocery store, ground-floor shops, and 83 apartments and townhomes per an NVRC document (Grosvenor's own project total is 82 homes — for the split).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Edgemont

items.t: District plans and zoning (District of North Vancouver — not the City): the Official Community Plan is Bylaw 7900, under which District growth is directed to its town and village centres, with Edgemont designated as one of the six village centres while surrounding established streets remain low-density. Suites: since June 2024, District zoning permits a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house — three units total — on all single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary; December 2023 changes let a secondary suite be up to 49% of the house with no minimum size and raised the maximum coach house height to two storeys. SSMUH: the District's GEOweb classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop; the Province's Bill 25 (November 2025) requires full SSMUH density by June 30, 2026, with the District's compliance amendments still in preparation in spring 2026. Hazard frame: Schedule B of the OCP establishes Development Permit Areas for Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard — Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek run through the neighbourhood's ravines.

District of North Vancouver property taxes: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value, and single-family utility fees include water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60 (combined single-family utilities $2,571 in 2026). Strata units carry their own utility arrangements — confirm on the Form B.

blocks.text: Good to know about Edgemont

items.t: Edgemont's entire condo supply stands on one crescent. All three verified buildings — Edgemont Villa (2003), Connaught (2019) and Crescentview (2023) — are on Connaught Crescent, a short walk apart beside the library, grocery and cafés. A "condos in Edgemont" search that returns anything on another street deserves a second look before a drive.

Connaught answers to two civic numbers and two project totals. Current unit listings use 3220 Connaught Crescent while the developer/presale sources use 3230 Connaught Crescent for the same project, and the totals run 82 homes (Grosvenor: 59 apartments + 23 townhomes) against 83 apartments and townhomes in an NVRC document. Settle the address and the unit's strata plan from the title and Form B, not from either marketing figure.

The village grocery site was rebuilt around the condos. The Grosvenor Edgemont project redeveloped the village's main grocery site at the Edgemont/Ridgewood gateway with an expanded grocery store (Thrifty Foods), ground-floor shops and its 82 condos and townhomes — the retail that Edgemont Villa, Crescentview and Amica residents walk to is this renewed core, not the strip it replaced.

The care ladder is in the same few blocks. A buyer can move from an owned suite at Edgemont Villa (Connaught Crescent) to rental independent/assisted/memory and licensed residential care at Amica Edgemont Village (3225 Highland Boulevard) without leaving the village — Amica is registered with the provincial Assisted Living Registry, operator Edgemont Senior Living Inc. (55+ notes

The elementary catchment split runs through the neighbourhood. The Highland Boulevard side samples to Canyon Heights Elementary and the Colwood Drive side to Highlands Elementary in the SD44 locator, both feeding Handsworth Secondary — a street-by-street fact that affects resale to families even for a buyer in the 55+ building thinking about exit value. No Connaught Crescent locator run is on record — do not assume which side of the split the condos fall on.

Creek ravines are a permit fact, not just scenery. Mosquito Creek and Mackay Creek run through Edgemont's ravines; District planning material describes Mosquito Creek as a "creekside natural area with well used trails" and MacKay Creek as a "creekside natural area with fish habitat," and the OCP's hazard Development Permit Areas (Streamside, Creek Hazard, Slope Hazard) apply to creek and slope lots.
There are no SnapStats numbers for North Vancouver.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Edgemont

Connaught (townhome component) — 3230 Connaught Crescent (project address per the developer/presale sources; current listings for individual units use 3220 Connaught Crescent — both numbers are in public use for the same project). STRATA — the townhome component of the project's strata; completed 2019; 23 townhomes

Grosvenor describes its Edgemont Village project, named Connaught, as 82 high-quality concrete condominiums and townhomes with ground-floor retail anchored by Thrifty Foods (Shoppers Drug Mart among the retailers), construction commenced 2016 and completed 2019 — the homes are resales, not presales. The form split is sourced, not estimated: a building-directory project source records the project as 59 apartments and 23 townhomes (82 total), reconciling with Grosvenor's own total; an NVRC document counts the wider grocery-site project at 83 apartments and townhomes — the one-home difference is not confirmed between those sources and does not affect the 23-townhome figure. No source states any age restriction — general-market, verified NOT 55+ in the 55-plus pass. Published pet position: a current listing for an apartment unit in the project records cats OK in listing data — carried as listing data for that unit, not as a project bylaw.
Edgemont Ridge Estates — 2425 Edgemont Boulevard. STRATA townhouse complex; built 1991.

Listing copy describes a gated community of one-level and multi-level residences with private rooftop decks / balconies and attached garages. Age restriction: no source states one — verified NOT 55+ in the 55-plus pass, and that position is unchanged by this upgrade, which is about form and tenure only.

items.t: Nearby areas: Canyon Heights (west), Capilano Highlands (north), Delbrook and Upper Lonsdale (east), Queensdale (southeast). The MLS sub-area name as the board (Greater Vancouver REALTORS®) uses it is Edgemont.

Where townhouse stock concentrates: in and immediately around the village core, in two places — Connaught Crescent (the Connaught project's 23 townhomes, beside its 59 apartments) and Edgemont Boulevard at the village's east side (Edgemont Ridge Estates, 2425 Edgemont Boulevard).

Recreation and hazards frame: Murdo Frazer Park is the Edgemont-area District park (6 tennis courts and 6 pickleball courts in the District's Outdoor Sports Courts Optimization Strategy, approved July 21, 2025); the Delbrook Community Recreation Centre, 851 West Queens Road, is the nearest NVRC full-service centre. Grouse Mountain (6400 Nancy Greene Way) and Capilano Suspension Bridge Park (3735 Capilano Road) are in neighbouring Upper Capilano. The District designates Natural Hazard Development Permit Areas for slope and creek hazards — Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek run through the neighbourhood's ravines.

The Grosvenor Edgemont project redeveloped the village's main grocery site at the Edgemont/Ridgewood gateway with an expanded grocery store (Thrifty Foods), ground-floor shops and its 82 condos and townhomes — the retail that Edgemont Villa, Crescentview, Connaught and Amica residents walk to is this renewed core, not the strip it replaced.

items.t: Fee-simple lots — the default form: mostly freehold detached; strata exists only in the village-core attached stock. A fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees. No bare-land strata development offered as vacant lots is verified for this ground.

Typical lot dimensions: Not verified from an official source, so no size is carried. Housing is a mix of original 1950s–60s houses, major renovations and new custom builds on the plateau streets (character; an age/style count is not verified).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Edgemont

items.t: Board position: "Edgemont" is the MLS sub-area name as the board (Greater Vancouver REALTORS) uses it. Nearby areas: Canyon Heights (west), Capilano Highlands (north), Delbrook and Upper Lonsdale (east), Queensdale (southeast).

The SnapStats GVR September 2026 report contains no North Vancouver section at all — its GVR communities are Burnaby, New Westminster, Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, Port Moody, Pitt Meadows and Maple Ridge.

Land shape: predominantly single-detached homes on sloped, view-capable lots on the plateau between the Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek ravines; attached housing concentrates in and immediately around the village core. District growth is directed to its town and village centres under the OCP, while surrounding established streets remain low-density.

Schools (SD44 North Vancouver, Ministry-listed names): Highlands Elementary (K–7, 3150 Colwood Drive) and Canyon Heights Elementary (K–7, 4501 Highland Boulevard) split the neighbourhood, feeding Handsworth Secondary (Grades 8–12, 1033 Handsworth Road). Catchments for other Edgemont addresses remain address-specific — not verified without a locator run for the exact address.

Recreation anchors: Murdo Frazer Park is the verified Edgemont-area District park (6 tennis courts and 6 pickleball courts in the District's Outdoor Sports Courts Optimization Strategy, approved July 21, 2025); the Delbrook Community Recreation Centre (851 West Queens Road) is the nearest NVRC full-service centre; Grouse Mountain (6400 Nancy Greene Way) and Capilano Suspension Bridge Park (3735 Capilano Road) sit in neighbouring Upper Capilano.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Edgemont

items.t: OCP — District of North Vancouver Official Community Plan Bylaw 7900, under which Edgemont is designated one of the District's six village centres and growth is directed to town and village centres.

Zoning — District of North Vancouver Zoning Bylaw 3210: — District numbers only; City of North Vancouver bylaws belong to the City and are never imported here. Any parcel's actual zone: per-parcel, not verified here.

Suites and coach houses — as the District states it: since June 2024, District zoning permits a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house — three units total — on all single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary; December 2023 changes let a secondary suite be up to 49% of the house with no minimum size and raised the maximum coach house height to two storeys.

SSMUH — as the District states it: the District's GEOweb SSMUH classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop. The Province's Bill 25 (November 2025) requires full SSMUH density by June 30, 2026; the District's compliance amendments were still in preparation in spring 2026, tied to the Zoning Bylaw Rewrite project, whose timeline extends into Q3 2027. Per-lot classification governs — check GEOweb for the exact lot.

Hazard permit areas: Schedule B of the District OCP establishes Development Permit Areas for Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard, and the District's GEOweb flood construction level data is defined as modelled flood water levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m. Creek-adjacent and steep lots warrant a GeoWeb check before pricing a renovation or rebuild — slope and creek DPAs can add geotechnical and permit cost.
Subdivision and servicing — District of North Vancouver servicing bylaw number not confirmed (held, never borrowed): (Standing verified ledger, applied by exclusion.)

Property taxes — District of North Vancouver (a municipality; follow its own research): 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value, and single-family utility fees include water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60 (combined single-family utilities $2,571 in 2026).

blocks.text: Good to know about Edgemont

items.t: No District park is named "Edgemont Park" (Nov 1, 2026). The research expressly records that no park by that name was found in District sources — Murdo Frazer Park is the verified Edgemont-area District park, described in a District planning table as "predominantly natural area and trails with some community uses (pitch and putt and tennis courts)." A listing that names "Edgemont Park" is naming something the District does not.

The flood construction level here is a 2100-horizon model (Nov 1, 2026). The District's GEOweb flood construction level data is defined as modelled flood water levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m — a future-climate figure, not a historical flood line, which changes how a creek-lot buyer should read it.
The village's main grocery site is the redevelopment (Nov 1, 2026).

The library is the civic anchor, in the village's heart (Nov 1, 2026). The Capilano Library at 3045 Highland Boulevard is described by the North Vancouver District Public Library as "located in the heart of Edgemont Village" and "a cornerstone of its community," with a quiet study room, storytimes and technology training — walkable-village claims hold only within a few blocks of this strip.
The creek greenways are OCP-critical environmental areas (1999, carried in the OCP).

faq.q: How many condo buildings does Edgemont Village actually have?
faq.a: Everything else in Edgemont is detached houses, plus the Amica care residence, which is rental.

faq.q: Is Connaught a presale I need to worry about completing?
faq.a: No. Grosvenor states construction commenced in 2016 and completed in 2019 — the homes are resales, so diligence is strata documents and building condition, not assignment or completion risk.

faq.q: What 55+ homes can I buy in Edgemont?
faq.a: On current evidence, one building: Edgemont Villa, 3151 Connaught Crescent — a 20-unit (listing-stated), freehold strata built in 2003, described across multiple listings as a boutique 55+ residence in the heart of the village. Confirm the exact age bylaw in the strata documents before an offer — the listing wording is not the bylaw.

faq.q: My spouse is under 55. Can we both live in Edgemont Villa?
faq.a: Under provincial strata rules, a younger spouse or partner of a resident who meets the age requirement (or holds a legacy exemption) is exempt. Live-in caregivers are also exempt, as are children under 19 in the resident's care and adult children the resident cared for before 19 — Regulation 7.01, expanded effective May 1, 2023.

faq.q: Can I rent out an Edgemont condo?
faq.a: Long-term: yes in law — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC; in a 55+ building the tenant still has to satisfy the age bylaw or an exemption. Short-term: stratas may still ban or limit it, and Crescentview's published policy states short-term rentals like Airbnb are not permitted — confirm the current bylaw on the Form B.

faq.q: How many townhouse complexes does Edgemont actually have?
faq.a: Everything else attached in the village is apartment condos on Connaught Crescent or the Amica care residence, which is rental.

faq.q: Is Edgemont Villa a townhouse complex? It keeps appearing in my townhouse search.
faq.a: It is the village's verified 55+ building (listing-stated; confirm the exact bylaw on the Form B) — a 55+ apartment, not a townhouse.

faq.q: Is Connaught a presale I need to worry about completing?
faq.a: No. Grosvenor states construction commenced in 2016 and completed in 2019 — the homes (59 apartments + 23 townhomes) are resales, so diligence is strata documents and building condition, not assignment or completion risk.
